quest.title: Leroy: Hangman's Noose
quest.description: You find yourselves near the Leroy residence again...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x150, Primogem x20, Mora x25000

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, look! Fresh Fish, and the floor looks clean too. Someone definitely just tidied up.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There's someone in Benoit's house for sure. Let's go over and listen.

dialogues.speaker: Athos
dialogues.text: ...He's right, he can't just disappear altogether. At the very least, he needs to be seen once in a while... out on a walk or something like that.

dialogues.speaker: Athos
dialogues.text: If nothing else, it'll stop the neighbors from calling the Maison Gardiennage — I'd rather not have the Special Patrol's Musketeers breathing down our necks.

dialogues.speaker: Morticia
dialogues.text: Dad, you really want to go out for a walk, don't you?

dialogues.speaker: Benoit Leroy
dialogues.text: C—Can I?

dialogues.speaker: Morticia
dialogues.text: Of course you can! Not only that, but we'd be delighted to come with you.

dialogues.speaker: Athos
dialogues.text: Careful now — don't let him use it as an opportunity to call for help. Those two weirdos have been watching this place like hawks...

dialogues.speaker: Morticia
dialogues.text: Dad won't do that, I'm sure.

dialogues.speaker: Morticia
dialogues.text: Dad, you wouldn't want the Maison Gardiennage to know...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...To know what!? Why are they speaking so quietly? Paimon can't hear a thing.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: They're about to come out.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, we need to move a bit further away. This time, we have to think of a way to speak with Benoit, right?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yup.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, let's scoot.

dialogues.speaker: Morticia
dialogues.text: How is it, Dad? Are you feeling any better now?

dialogues.speaker: Benoit Leroy
dialogues.text: It's you!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Benoit...

dialogues.speaker: Benoit Leroy
dialogues.text: ...Help me! Uh, I mean, don't help me...

dialogues.speaker: Morticia
dialogues.text: What are you saying, Dad? What's all this "help me, don't help me" business? Hehe.

dialogues.speaker: Morticia
dialogues.text: Oh, it's you two. No wonder Dad went out of his way to talk to you — you are acquainted, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Benoit Leroy
dialogues.text: ...N—No, I don't! We don't know each other at all!

dialogues.speaker: Morticia
dialogues.text: No? But why would they be waiting here just for you then, Dad?

dialogues.speaker: Morticia
dialogues.text: They were even nice enough to get the paper for us. Why, they even went to the Fleuve Cendre to talk to our old neighbor, Snodgrass.

dialogues.speaker: Morticia
dialogues.text: I think you must be very close! And no wonder. You've always loved kids, haven't you, Dad?

dialogues.speaker: Morticia
dialogues.text: I love kids too! But I'm afraid I'm not as selfless as my father. I love my own child the most, but... she's gone.

response.speaker: Morticia
response.text: Athos and I are our father's children. Dad loves us, and we love him too. Isn't it obvious?

response.speaker: Athos
response.text: Morticia, look at how lovely the weather is today. Perfect for a walk.

response.speaker: Morticia
response.text: So it is, Athos.

response.speaker: Athos
response.text: Have you seen today's Steambird? There are quite a few interesting stories.

response.speaker: Morticia
response.text: Oh dear, I fear I haven't.

response.speaker: Athos
response.text: There's one in particular about an old man who met an unfortunate end. Apparently, he encountered some thieves, and as there was no one by his side looking out for him, he ended up falling off a cliff and died.

response.speaker: Morticia
response.text: Oh, really? The horror! That's so terrible.

response.speaker: Athos
response.text: And another about a very unlucky merchant who drowned. It seems he drank too much, and walked into a lake in a stupor, and just like that... he drowned.

response.speaker: Morticia
response.text: Ah! My word! Truly unlucky!

response.speaker: Athos
response.text: #And this last one is very interesting! It's about a meddling busybody who just couldn't keep their nose out of other people's business. *sigh* {M#He}{F#She} accidentally took the wrong medicine.

response.speaker: Athos
response.text: #{M#He}{F#She} mistook poison for medicine for {M#his}{F#her} illness, and just like that, swallowed the lot! And then ended up dying very, very painfully.

response.speaker: Morticia
response.text: Oh my! There really are so many ways to die. Please, go on.

response.speaker: Benoit Leroy
response.text: ...Sorry, sorry! I won't ever do that again.

response.speaker: Morticia
response.text: What ever are you talking about, Dad? We're not trying to say it's your fault or anything. But... you must be tired after running around so much.

response.speaker: Morticia
response.text: Athos, why don't we go back and read the newspaper to Dad? You subscribe to a lot of papers, don't you, Dad?

response.speaker: Athos
response.text: That's right! We've been chatting long enough. We ought to go back now.

response.speaker: Morticia
response.text: Let's go back together, Daddy dearest.

response.speaker: Morticia
response.text: Do you mean accompanying our dad on a walk? It's our duty as his children to do so, is it not? Failing such a basic responsibility to him would be a poor way to repay the care he has given us.

talks.objective: Observe what's going on near Benoit's residence

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Something's fishy, something's fishy... Even Paimon can tell that there's something off about all this!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, you're the brighter spark here. What should we do next?

choices.text: Benoit wants help but insists that he doesn't...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Then how about we go take another look near Benoit's house? Wasn't there a strange box by his back window?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: There's definitely something hidden in there, and it might just be the proof you're looking for...

choices.text: That couple may have come from the Fleuve Cendre...
From their reactions, I'd say that there are some hidden factors at work...
I have some theories, but no evidence to back them up.

talks.objective: Go and examine the strange box
Go and examine the strange box

dialogues.speaker: Athos
dialogues.text: Considering how persistent you two are, I didn't expect you to just leave it at that.

dialogues.speaker: Athos
dialogues.text: I thought you'd go running to the Maison Gardiennage, but you didn't. Looks like you have a few ideas of your own.

choices.text: Why are you keeping Benoit here?

response.speaker: Athos
response.text: To tell you the truth, you've impressed me quite a bit. If you'd only put your enthusiasm to better use, you'd have bright futures ahead of you.

response.speaker: Athos
response.text: It's just a shame that you won't be getting anywhere with this. *sigh* You really aren't afraid, are you?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You picked the wrong person to intimidate.

response.speaker: Athos
response.text: Oh? So do you really not have a clue what's going on here, or is it because you think you're on the side of justice?

response.speaker: Athos
response.text: Incidentally, there was an article recently about a merchant who drowned — his name was Brandt. That fellow sure had a way with words alright...

response.speaker: Athos
response.text: Guess what? According to the paper, it turns out he didn't drown after all, but was in fact murdered and thrown into the lake.

response.speaker: Athos
response.text: After a very long investigation, all that the Marechaussee Phantom was able to conclude was that he was murdered, and that the murderer was guilty of a heinous crime.

response.speaker: Athos
response.text: So that's what the news report said. Who knows what actually happened, or even which one of them deserved to die more — the murderer, or the victim?

response.speaker: Athos
response.text: Hmm... A tough question, isn't it? I haven't decided what the answer is yet either.

response.speaker: Athos
response.text: Anyway, I digress! This has nothing to do with what we need to discuss.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What are you trying to say?

response.speaker: Athos
response.text: I'm saying that acting recklessly before you've fully understood a situation is foolish, and might bring about some undesirable consequences.

choices.text: Witnessing injustice and doing nothing... That is true folly.

response.speaker: Athos
response.text: Haha... Well, perhaps if we'd met under different circumstances, we'd be friends.

response.speaker: Athos
response.text: Though I like the way you think, I have things to do.

response.speaker: Athos
response.text: This is as far as my patience can be stretched. Next time I see you two anywhere near my house, I'll do something about it — mark my words.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: After muttering something inexplicable, Athos leaves.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: His bizarre attitude surprises you, and you start to wonder what position you should take in the matter...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You suddenly hear a faint tapping sound coming from the back window, and then after a barely audible creak, a note drops down from the window...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: There is brown writing on the note. It looks like someone wrote it in a real hurry, and it appears that they used coffee to do so...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Quick, see what it says!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's Benoit!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Shh!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Sorry! Anyway, let's keep an eye out for the food bowl and wait for his signal.

choices.text: Whenever I witness injustice, I take action.
How are you two actually related to Benoit?
